input:
Administration: click "Permission", rage x5
Claims: click "Save"
The user is frustrated by having to click the Permission button repeatedly.

Great. And how do you ... handle document versioning? We’ve lost track of updates before.
The customer cannot keep track of document version updates.

That’s a relief — we’ve had issues with supplier letters not triggering automatically, and it’s causing delays in task assignments.
Supplier letters are not triggering automatically, which delays task assignments.

the permission setup is taking ages — each user needs dozens of boxes ticked manually and if we miss one, they get locked out.
Manually configuring permissions for each new user is slow and prone to errors, causing lockouts.

We’re getting heat ... because the system isn’t handling joint policyholder names correctly — it’s pulling in just one, and that’s triggering formal complaints.
The system only captures one joint policyholder name, causing complaints from policyholders.

I’m trying to pull the latest reserves report for Brackwater Homecover but the system’s throwing an error when I filter by supplier payments.
The system throws an error when filtering the reserves report by supplier payments.

That’s the issue — ... I’ll pull the ... cases for you.
The system failed to route letters correctly due to policyholder status or document tag issues.

Appreciate that — we need to reduce those delays before next quarter’s audit.
The customer is experiencing delays that could affect the upcoming audit.

We’re evaluating whether the tiered pricing model fits our claims volume, especially with seasonal spikes... are we locked into the current payment integration?
The customer is unsure if the tiered pricing works for their fluctuating claim volume and worries they may be stuck with the current payment integration.

We’re handling 200+ claims a week—manual edits aren’t scalable.
Manual edits to claim letters are not scalable for high claim volumes.

Perfect, thanks. One last thing — I think my login credentials expired. Can you help me reset them?
The user cannot log in because their credentials have expired.

Also, can we confirm the payment status is syncing correctly with our suppliers after a reserve update?
The user is unsure whether the payment status syncs correctly with suppliers after a reserve update.

Reports: click "Save", rage x3
Saving reports causes repeated rage due to failures.

we’re getting complaints because our letters to joint policyholders only show one name — it’s causing confusion and we need this fixed.
Letters to joint policyholders only display a single name, causing confusion.

we’ve been having some trouble with joint policyholder names in outgoing letters
Difficulty handling joint policyholder names in outgoing letters.

We’ve got a few joint ... cases where the letters are ... coming out with mismatched names—causing complaints.
Letters are being generated with mismatched policyholder names, leading to complaints.

The issue with letters merging multiple names on letters is causing us real problems — clients are complaining because only one name shows up, and sometimes it’s not even the right one... It’s not just awkward, it’s damaging our client trust.
Letters that merge multiple names only display a single, often incorrect, name, leading to client complaints and loss of trust.

are tasks auto-assigned when letters go out to policyholders? We’re seeing delays.
Tasks are not being auto-assigned when letters are sent, causing delays.

Morning Bryn, I’m setting up our new claims team and the permissions system is causing delays — it’s tedious and error-prone.
The permissions system is slowing down the setup of the new claims team because it is tedious and error‑prone.

Can we export our case notes as PDFs? It’s for audit purposes. We need to be able to export notes as PDF for compliance and internal review — it’s not just convenience, it’s required for our monthly audits.
The platform does not currently allow exporting case notes as PDFs, which is needed for audit and compliance.

Hi Bryn, we’re setting up a new claims team and the permission setup duplication is slowing us down — can we get help?
Duplicating permission setup tasks is slowing down the creation of a new claims team.

I’m writing to request an update to the purchase order number on your invoice — this is causing reconciliation issues, and I need the invoice contact change reflected accurately in our records.
The invoice has an incorrect purchase order number, causing reconciliation issues for the customer.

Just need to know when we can expect the joint policyholder names to appear correctly in correspondence.
Joint policyholder names are not showing correctly in generated correspondence.

It’s frustrating because bounced payments mean we’re reissuing them days later, which messes up our reserves and reporting.
Bounced payments force reissuing days later, disrupting reserves and reporting.

Hi Bryn, I’m having trouble pulling the latest supplier reports into the system — any idea what might be blocking it?
The user cannot pull the latest supplier reports into the system.

Claims: click "Details" ... Claims: click "Save", rage x3
The Save action is flaky, forcing users to click multiple times and get angry.

We’re running into delays because the payee account verification step isn’t happening before the payment is sent out, which causes rework and client frustration.
Delays occur because payee account verification is not performed before the payment is sent, leading to rework and client frustration.

We’re setting up a new team for claims handling and the permission setup is taking ages — each user needs dozens of boxes ticked manually and if we miss one, they get locked out.
Configuring permissions for each new user is slow and error‑prone, leading to lockouts.

Hi Bryn, I’m Mavren from Merrow Vale Motor — I’m locked out of our claims portal and need to reset my password urgently.
The user is locked out of the claims portal and cannot log in.

I’m trying to reconcile the reserves for two recent claims at Elderfold Home, but the figures aren’t matching up with our internal spreadsheets.
The claim reserve numbers do not match the company's internal spreadsheets.

I just spent 45 minutes ticking boxes for one person. ... I can’t just duplicate an existing role — I have to manually select permissions for each new user, and if I make a mistake, it locks them out of their tasks.
Admins must manually configure permissions for each new user because roles cannot be duplicated, leading to wasted time and risk of locking users out.

Can you walk me through the steps for payee account verification? I need to ensure the supplier’s banking details are correctly flagged before issuing the payment.
The user doesn't know how to verify a payee's banking details before making a payment.

That’s exactly what we need — especially with supplier integrations and reporting getting more complex each quarter.
Supplier integrations and reporting are becoming increasingly complex each quarter.

we need to copy access roles, not rebuild them from scratch every time
Users have to recreate access roles manually for each new user.

I need to reset my password because I’m locked out of the claims dashboard and can’t access policyholder documents.
The user is locked out of the claims dashboard and cannot view policyholder documents because they need a password reset.

I need to reset my password for accessing the claims portal — can you guide me through that?
The user cannot log into the claims portal because they need to reset their password.

I can’t just copy the permissions from our existing role, so I’m having to click through every box for each person... I’m terrified I’ll lock someone out by accident. We really need to copy access roles, not rebuild them from scratch every time.
Users cannot copy permissions from an existing role and must manually set each permission, risking errors.

I’m trying to get a batch of claims documents uploaded and linked to the right reserves, but I’m not sure where the task queue sits in the interface.
The customer cannot find the task queue in the interface while trying to upload and link a batch of claims documents.

can we generate letters automatically based on claim status? We’re drowning in manual correspondence.
The team is overwhelmed by having to create and send letters manually for each claim status.

We’ve been getting complaints because when ... letters go out for policies with two named holders, the system only ... includes one name — and sometimes it’s the wrong ...
Letters for joint policies only include one holder's name, often the wrong one.

Appreciate that — we really need this sorted before the next claims batch goes out.
The joint policyholder names issue remains unresolved.

We need to adjust the purchase order reference on the invoice you sent — it’s causing reconciliation problems with our finance team, and we’re hoping you can help with the purchase order correction.
The invoice has an incorrect purchase order reference that is causing finance reconciliation issues.

That’s a relief. We’ve been trying to automate those letters and hit a wall with the current defaults.
The customer cannot automate letters because the default templates are insufficient.

Sure — every time we issue payments to third-party suppliers, we can’t validate their bank details ahead of time, which means payments bounce and we’re stuck reissuing days later.
They cannot validate third‑party suppliers' bank details before issuing payments, causing bounced payments and delayed re‑issuance.

we need something that doesn’t force us to change how we work
The current solution forces them to alter their existing workflow.

Just one more thing — are there any upcoming updates to the suppliers section? We’re hoping to streamline our vendor payments soon.
The customer needs upcoming updates to the suppliers section to improve vendor payment processes.

Appreciate it — we’ve had two handlers locked out already this week just from missing a checkbox.
Handlers are getting locked out because they miss a required checkbox.

I’m having trouble uploading the policyholder documents for claim A13 — they keep failing validation.
The user cannot upload policyholder documents because they fail validation.

Can you walk me through how to attach documents to a claim? I keep missing a step.
The user cannot successfully attach documents to a claim because they keep missing a step.

we’re trying to streamline our claims handling and need help filtering tasks by due date.
They cannot easily filter claim tasks by due date, making claims handling inefficient.

Can you walk me through how to update the reserves section after a supplier payment has been confirmed?
The user does not know how to update the reserves after confirming a supplier payment.

Perfect — I’ll have my team pull the last three months’ claims logs so you can compare against the system’s reporting output.
The customer lacks an easy way to verify that the platform's reporting matches the actual claims logs.

I’m especially keen to see how your system handles documents and reserves together without manual juggling.
The team has to manually juggle documents and reserves when processing claims.

Reports: click "Save", rage x3
Saving reports causes repeated rage due to failures.

Also, can you confirm if our supplier payments are synced with the latest integrations?
The customer is unsure whether their supplier payments are synchronized with the latest integrations.

We’re seeing a problem where letters sent to joint policyholders merge only one name — this synonym ‘multiple names on letters’ is critical because clients are complaining and it’s hurting our reputation.
Letters to joint policyholders only include one name, causing client complaints and reputational damage.

We’ve had to reissue payments multiple times — it’s eating into our reserves and slowing reporting... payment detail checking isn’t possible before sending out funds, which leads to bounced payments and delays in reissuing them — it’s affecting our reserves and supplier relationships.
The platform doesn't allow payment detail verification before sending funds, causing bounced payments and costly reissues.

The setup process is a pain because you can’t copy access roles — every new team member means manually selecting permissions one by one, and if you make a mistake, the handler gets locked out until it’s corrected.
Manually assigning permissions for each new user is time‑consuming and errors lock handlers out of the system.

we can’t verify third-party bank info before paying — so payments bounce and we reissue days later... we’re currently facing delays because we can’t validate third-party bank details before sending payments — that’s why we’re reissuing them days later
They cannot verify third‑party bank information before issuing payments, causing bounced payments and costly re‑issuances.

We’re stuck because we can’t copy access roles — every new handler needs permissions ticked individually, and if we slip up, they’re locked out of their tasks.
Admins must manually assign permissions to each new handler, which is time‑consuming and error‑prone, causing lockouts.

And what about roles? We’ve got adjusters, supervisors, and external auditors — can permissions be granular?
The customer needs fine‑grained permission controls for different user roles.

The PO we referenced doesn’t match what’s on your billing, and it’s blocking our payment cycle.
The purchase order they referenced does not match the billing information, which is halting their payment process.

We’re manually editing the letters before sending, but it’s time-consuming and prone to error with joint policyholder names.
Manually editing letters before sending is time‑consuming and leads to errors, especially with joint policyholder names.

The permission setup duplication is a real bottleneck — every new user means manually selecting permissions, and one slip can lock someone out of their claims tasks.
Manually setting permissions for each new user is time‑consuming and error‑prone, causing bottlenecks.
